speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to narrow down the cause, have you noticed any fever, chills, or nausea accompanying these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given your history of recurrent urinary tract infections and visible blood in the urine, have you noticed any difficulty passing urine, such as a weak stream, pain during urination, or the passage of small, pebble-like stones?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Renal Cell Carcinoma

The presence of painless hematuria (or hematuria with flank pain) combined with a history of recurrent UTIs is highly suspicious for a renal mass rather than a simple stone or infection. Given the potential seriousness of this finding, I need to visualize the kidney immediately.

REQUEST IMAGES: Renal Ultrasound and CT Abdomen with Contrast.
